justifications.c1: There is no loss figure. The only money items are a c.2018 non-UK vendor notice of a 180% FM-200 price rise and a £50k public tender for a whole system (purchase cost, not a loss). No refill cost per cylinder or failed-suppression loss was found.
justifications.c2: The check recurs only every six months (BS EN 15004, via secondary summaries; the Designing Buildings page was found, but its 5%/semi-annual detail was not seen in search). No statistic was found on how often cylinders fail the 5% test, so leak events are unquantified.
justifications.c3: The workaround is documented: a 6-monthly contractor visit with weighing or ultrasonic level checks (Coltraco Portalevel, Parr 'gas supply integrity testing'). No labour time or price was found, and the visit stays mandatory regardless.
justifications.c4: F-gas rules require leak checks and records (GOV.UK, NetRegs: 12-monthly, or 24 with leak detection), and EN 15004 requires semi-annual contents checks. However, the FIA says EN 15004/ISO 14520 servicing is deemed to satisfy F-gas (search-confirmed), so continuous monitoring is not required, and no enforcement was found.
justifications.c5: The only buyer evidence is public tenders and a directory of BAFE SP203-3 contractors. No facilities or data-centre manager title with a suppression budget was found.
justifications.c6: BAFE SP203-3 contractors visit twice a year and bundle 'gas supply integrity testing' (Parr, Protec). They install suppression systems and panels, which is adjacent technology, but there is no evidence they resell continuous contents monitoring.
justifications.c7: Suppression-specific incumbents exist: Coltraco Permalevel Featherweight (1% leak flag, up to 48 cylinders, search-confirmed), TLX/Thames-side weighing, NAFFCO, Rotarex and a Kidde-Fenwal patent. No prices or customer counts were found, and the gap (price, cloud reporting) is only asserted.
justifications.c8: No load-cell or transducer prices were found. Load platforms under heavy cylinders are a custom mechanical job, and adding a transducer to a listed system may affect FM/LPCB approval, which is unresolved. The plant room may also trap RF.
justifications.c9: F-gas records are kept for 5 years, but the guidance's fire-protection scope is unconfirmed and EN 15004 servicing already satisfies it. Leak detection halving F-gas checks matters little, and no comparable subscription price was found.
justifications.c10: WorkSafe WA bulletins (Australian regulator, about actuator failure rather than leaks), a 1987 US nuclear LER, one Eng-Tips forum thread and Novec phase-out vendor content. None is UK, and none shows that slow leaks are a recurring pain.

weakest: There is no sourced money loss or leak-frequency data, and the FIA says the existing 6-monthly EN 15004 service already satisfies F-gas, so continuous monitoring is neither required nor shown to save money.
